name: Rochester Gas and Electric Corporation
territory: Nine-county region centred on Rochester, NY
filing_case: Case 25-E-0379 (temporary rates Jun 2026; final order pending)
_dc_note: Upstate NY data centre load estimated at ~300 MW (2026) reflecting 179% increase in requested MVA at RG&E 2022-2024 per Avangrid SCC testimony. Growth rate 5%/yr reflects projects already approved and under construction proceeding, constrained by Governor Hochul's May 2026 moratorium on new data centres over 50 MW. Source: Avangrid 'Powering New York' SCC presentation July 2025; NY Executive Order No. 62 June 2026.
_sources: Rate base, annual_capex_m and total_revenue_m are ESTIMATED, back-calculated from the June 2025 filing under NYPSC Case 25-E-0379. PSC set temporary rates June 1 2026 (+4.0% electric); final order still pending — update these figures when the final order is issued. ROE is the utility's requested rate (10.0%), not yet approved. Data centre load parameters reflect upstate NY DC siting activity.
_notes: capacity_market / capacity_market_zone are descriptive metadata pointing to shared/capacity_markets/NYISO.json; not yet consumed by the model engine at this refactoring stage — CAPACITY_COST_START remains a notebook-level global.
_class_shares_note: EIA Form 861, 2024 (Sales_Ult_Cust_2024.xlsx), Rochester Gas & Electric Corp, NY: bundled (Part A) + delivery-only (Part C) rows, so retail-choice load is included. Residential sales 2,842,349 of 6,871,716 MWh = 41.4%; residential customers 351,481 of 392,342 = 89.6%. Used only when CAPACITY_SAVINGS_ALLOCATION = 'sales_share' (CORRECTED): the residential capacity credit is scaled by sales share / customer share.

forward_assumptions._note: Forward assumptions for the layer engine (engine/layers.py). v1.0 / CORRECTED do not read this section. Levels: for layer assumptions 'low' gives customers a SMALLER shared-savings effect and 'high' a LARGER one. For growth assumptions (projection, system_needs, capacity price growth) low/high = lower/higher growth. Scenarios (Cautious / Central / Ambitious) set the programs, deferral and utilisation layers together and hold growth assumptions and the utility share at central.

Cautious.description: Low flexible MW and EE savings, high cost per kW-year, high capitalised share, low locational match and utilisation; growth and utility share central.

Ambitious.description: High flexible MW and EE savings, low cost per kW-year, low capitalised share, high locational match and utilisation; growth and utility share central.

supply_energy_growth.source: Assumption: central = INFLATION_RATE (flat real energy prices)

transmission_growth.source: Assumption: central = INFLATION_RATE; high reflects transmission build-out

program_surcharge_growth.source: Assumption: BAU surcharge rates grow with inflation (policy-driven)

ev_share_of_electrification.source: NREL Electrification Futures Study: transportation is 1,424 of 1,782 TWh (80%) of the 2050 increase in the High scenario and 810 of 932 TWh (87%) in Medium
ev_share_of_electrification.note: Reconciliation: the notebook ramp is TOTAL electrification (its sources cite EVs and heat pumps). It is split 80% EVs / 20% buildings and other using the EFS High-scenario sector split, so both segments contribute and total electrification equals the v1.0 load forecast. The EV count curve is no longer used for energy (at 3,600 kWh/EV it implied more energy than the whole ramp for Con Edison, RG&E and Pepco).

capacity_carve_out.source: NYISO Rest of State (RG&E is in Load Zone B) monthly spot capacity prices, 2026: May $8.00, Jul $4.14, Sep $5.97/kW-month (Modo Energy NYISO monthly reports); mean $6.0367/kW-month x 12 = $0.07244M/MW-yr. v1.0 uses NYISO.json zone G_H_I ($0.070M/MW-yr) for RG&E; that default is unchanged. Peak: RGE.json. Residential share and customers: EIA-861 2024. Scaling 1.0 (NYISO reserve margin not applied).
capacity_carve_out.method: Residential capacity obligation per customer = peak_mw x residential_share x obligation_scaling / residential_customers; $/month = obligation (kW) x price ($/kW-day) x 365/12. Assumes the residential share of the obligation equals its share of sales (residential load is peakier, so this likely understates it). The amount is moved out of the parent line(s); the total bill is unchanged.
